subject: Post-call: SignalFlow eval — sample collection + model-fit thresholds
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@signalflow.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: SignalFlow eval — sample collection + model-fit thresholds

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have clear scope for a short evaluation run: 

1) Goal: Verify model fit for SignalFlow’s QA assistant (customer support triage + policy citation) across: accuracy of citation, hallucination rate, and redaction safety.
2) Deliverables from SignalFlow: a) ~200 representative prompts (mix of live user queries, edge cases, escalation cases), b) a short list of high-risk fields (PII patterns), and c) any sample conversation context we should preserve.
3) What Redwood will provide: initial model recommendations and a small-scale benchmark (100 evals) with latency/cost estimates and a quality regression baseline.
4) Timeline: if we get samples by next Tuesday (5/11), we can run the pilot and share results by 5/18.

Ask: can you send a CSV with the prompt text + context indicator + sensitivity tag? Example column headers we used: id, prompt_text, user_role, channel, sensitivity_level. If helpful, I attached a lightweight template in the body below.

Template (paste into CSV):
- id: sf-001
- prompt_text: "How do I reset my API key?"
- user_role: customer
- channel: web
- sensitivity_level: low

Quick notes on redaction and edge cases: please include examples that expose long context dependencies (multi-turn), and any example where the correct answer requires citing a specific policy section. Also flag prompts that include user-supplied snippets (uploads) — we’ll need to treat those as sensitive.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 15-min sync if that helps.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam@signalflow.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: SignalFlow Eng <eng@signalflow.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SignalFlow eval — sample collection + model-fit thresholds

Thanks Marcus — that recap looks right. Attaching an initial batch (30 rows) so you can get started. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We included real anonymized queries from the last quarter; some still contain partial PII (order numbers, abbreviated email fragments). We can scrub further if you prefer.
- Major concern is "policy drift" — when the model returns a plausible answer but cites the wrong internal policy. We'd like to measure citation accuracy separately from factual correctness.
- Also interested in a stress test for chained reasoning: multi-turn where the user refers back to previous messages.

Attachment: signalflow_prompt_samples.csv (30 rows) — columns: id, prompt_text, context_history, expected_action, sensitivity_flag.

Can you also share which open models you think are good starting points? We're trying to avoid a full private deployment initially; prefer a hosted pilot if latency is acceptable.

Sam
Sam Patel

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SignalFlow eval — sample collection + model-fit thresholds

Looping in recommended starting points so Sam has clarity:

- For a citation-heavy QA workflow we usually recommend: gpt-open-7b-qp (quantized path) for fast dev iteration, and gpt-open-13b-v2 for the first quality baseline. These balance cost and ability to preserve citations with proper prompt engineering.
- Evaluation plan (short): 100 seeded prompts from their sample CSV covering low/medium/high sensitivity buckets; metrics = citation_precision, hallucination_rate, exact-action-match, avg_latency@p95.
- Quick benchmark link: https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/benchmarks/signalflow-quickstart.md (reads-only) — includes our runbook and metric definitions.

Action items for Redwood (Ben/Marcus/Irene):
- Marcus: run config recommendations and a cost estimate for both models (dev vs baseline).
- Irene: prepare a lightweight eval harness (Jenkins job + results dashboard) and a regression guardrail set that flags quality drops on citation_precision.
- Sam: confirm whether you want us to scrub your CSV further or if you’ll provide a redacted batch.

I added a short bench plan to the Drive link. If they prefer hosted pilot we can route to our dedicated pool for predictable latency.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Sam Patel <sam@signalflow.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SignalFlow eval — sample collection + model-fit thresholds

Thanks all — plan sounds good. Sam, two quick asks before we kick the run: 

1) Edge-case capture: can you add 20 examples where the correct answer requires citing a specific policy paragraph (e.g., "see Policy §4.2") and mark them sensitivity_level=high? Those will be used to compute citation_precision.

2) Redaction guidance: attached a short checklist we use when ingesting customer prompts. If you can pre-redact order numbers and long raw user uploads, that will speed the pilot. If you cannot share redacted data, we can run the eval in a private deployment and show redacted-only outputs to SignalFlow.

Logistics: I’ll circulate a short readout template after the run: overall metrics, top 10 failure cases, suggested prompt engineering tweaks, and a one-slide recommendation (dev model vs baseline model + rough cost delta).

Next meeting: propose Tue 5/18 10:00am PT for a 30-min readout (I’ll send a calendar invite once we have results).

Thanks — forwarding the redaction checklist now.

— Marcus
